hook: Conductive polymer dye turns hair into an EEG electrode that records stronger signals without gel
hook_turn: that records stronger signals without gel
summary: Researchers coated hair with conductive polythiophene polymer dyes so that strands form low-impedance contact with the scalp. EEG recordings showed higher signal amplitude and spectral power while preserving neural dynamics, and hair-based transistors amplified signals locally. The abstract gives no sample size or long-term wear data, so durability and performance across hair types are unclear.
title: Electronic hair: Transforming hair into a scalable bioelectronic interface.
